reconstructed_theorem_text:
Objects: For n in N put t[n,i]=i*T/2^n for i=0,...,2^n, and Delta_i^n Z=Z(t[n,i+1])-Z(t[n,i]). The vector Brownian hypothesis means B(0,omega)=0 for every omega; increments on finite families of pairwise disjoint half-open intervals are jointly independent; every continuous real linear functional ell sends B(t)-B(s), s<t, to a centered Gaussian of variance (t-s)||ell||^2; paths are mu-almost surely continuous. B is strongly adapted, and for every s<=t the increment B(t)-B(s) is independent of the sigma-algebra filtration(s). Let Delta_i^n B_j=B_j(t[n,i+1],omega)-B_j(t[n,i],omega).

Domains: Omega measurable; kappa finite with decidable equality; mu a measure (no finite-measure instance is stated); filtration on R_+; B:R_+ x Omega->R^kappa; distinct j,k in kappa; T>=0; weight a_n,i:Omega->R for n in N and 0<=i<2^n; C real.

Quantifiers: Universally Omega,kappa,instances,filtration,mu,B,hB,j,k,hjk,T,weight,hAdapted,hWeight,C,hC. The weight hypotheses hold for every n and every i; then n tends to infinity.

Assumptions: The vector Brownian properties just described hold. j!=k. Every a_n,i is strongly measurable with respect to the left-endpoint sigma-algebra filtration(t[n,i]), and belongs to L^2(mu). There is one given C with integral a_n,i^2 dmu<=C for all n,i.

Conclusion: The real numbers integral_Omega (sum_{i=0}^{2^n-1} a_n,i(omega)*Delta_i^n B_j(omega)*Delta_i^n B_k(omega))^2 dmu tend to zero as n->infinity.

Scopes: The asserted convergence is of these second-moment integral values. No separate integrability statement for each full squared sum is printed. T may be zero. No usual-conditions or finite-mu assumption is separately included.

Constant dependencies: C is a single uniform bound independent of n and i; it can depend on the already chosen family of weights and preceding data. No explicit convergence rate is stated.
